title: Full blood count
subtitle: Haemoglobin, indices, white cells, differential and platelets
summary: Haemoglobin, indices, white cells, differential and platelets
introduction: Interpret haemoglobin, cell size, white-cell differential and platelets together. Typical ranges below are approximate adult examples and must be replaced by the reporting laboratory’s range.

rows.name: Haemoglobin
lowInterpretation: Anaemia. Assess magnitude, speed of fall, bleeding, haemolysis, renal disease, nutritional deficiency and chronic inflammation.
highInterpretation: Haemoconcentration from reduced plasma volume, smoking or chronic hypoxia; less commonly a primary erythrocytosis.

rows.name: MCV
lowInterpretation: Microcytosis: iron deficiency, thalassaemia or some chronic inflammatory states.
highInterpretation: Macrocytosis: vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis or medication effects.

rows.name: MCH / MCHC
lowInterpretation: Supports hypochromia, commonly seen with iron deficiency.
highInterpretation: MCH may rise with macrocytosis. A markedly raised MCHC can reflect spherocytosis, cold agglutinins or analytical interference.

rows.name: RDW
highInterpretation: Greater variation in red-cell size; may support evolving iron, B12 or folate deficiency, mixed deficiencies or recent transfusion.

rows.name: Total WCC
lowInterpretation: Viral illness, medication or chemotherapy effect, marrow suppression, autoimmune disease or severe sepsis.
highInterpretation: Infection, inflammation, corticosteroids, physiological stress, smoking or haematological disease.

rows.name: Neutrophils
lowInterpretation: Infection risk rises as the count falls. In a patient receiving anticancer treatment, neutrophils ≤0.5 ×10⁹/L with temperature >38°C or features of sepsis is neutropenic sepsis.
highInterpretation: Common with bacterial infection, inflammation, corticosteroids, tissue injury or physiological stress.

rows.name: Lymphocytes
lowInterpretation: Acute illness, corticosteroids, immunodeficiency or treatment effect.
highInterpretation: Often viral infection; persistent or marked elevation may require assessment for lymphoproliferative disease.

rows.name: Eosinophils
highInterpretation: Allergy, asthma, parasitic infection, drug reaction, eosinophilic disease or adrenal insufficiency.

rows.name: Platelet count
lowInterpretation: Bleeding risk depends on count, trajectory and platelet function. Consider sepsis, medication, liver disease, immune destruction, DIC or marrow failure.
highInterpretation: Reactive inflammation, infection, iron deficiency, recent surgery or splenectomy; persistent unexplained elevation may reflect a myeloproliferative disorder.

urgentFindings: Active bleeding, haemodynamic compromise, chest pain, syncope or breathlessness with anaemia.
Rapid haemoglobin fall compared with recent results, even when the current value remains within the laboratory range.
Neutrophils ≤0.5 ×10⁹/L with temperature >38°C or features of sepsis (for example hypotension, new confusion, rigors, reduced urine output or mottled skin) during anticancer treatment.
Platelets very low or falling with spontaneous bleeding, petechiae, melaena, haematuria, neurological symptoms or suspected DIC.
Pancytopenia: low haemoglobin, white cells and platelets together, particularly when new.
overrides: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference ranges and compare with previous results, symptoms, observations, medication and fluid status.
